title: React Project-Based Learning Applied Check
description: Apply project planning and implementation judgment to realistic requirements, milestones, architecture, edge cases, and tradeoffs.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: A Todo app accepts empty items because the input handler only checks for `value !== null`. What should the project do?

options.text: Trim input and reject empty text before adding
Store empty todos and hide them with CSS
Move validation to the list item component only

questions.explanation: The Todo project edge cases include preventing blank or whitespace-only todos.

questions.prompt: A weather app search for "Paris" returns after a later search for "Tokyo" and overwrites the UI. What pattern addresses this?

options.text: Ignore stale responses or track the current request
Render both cities in the same field

questions.explanation: Handling stale responses is an explicit async edge case in the weather project.

questions.prompt: A cart total is calculated with floating-point math and displayed with inconsistent cents. What should you consider?

options.text: Represent money carefully, such as cents integers or deliberate rounding

questions.explanation: The e-commerce cart lesson calls out money and rounding as a common source of mistakes.

questions.prompt: A full-stack project API contract should clarify which details? (Select all that apply.)
questions.explanation: API contracts define data and failure behavior between frontend and backend.

questions.prompt: A team starts with persistence, auth, charts, and animations before a basic project flow works. What project-planning issue is this?

options.text: Skipping milestones and overloading the first increment

questions.explanation: Milestones should get a basic vertical slice working before layering extensions.

questions.prompt: A project requirement says "users can remove cart items," but the acceptance criteria never mentions empty-cart UI. What should you add?

options.text: A clear expected empty-cart state after the last item is removed

questions.explanation: Acceptance criteria should include edge states that users can reach.

questions.prompt: A capstone reflection explains why Context was used instead of Redux for a small cart. What makes that reflection valuable?

options.text: It documents tradeoffs and scope-based reasoning
It proves Redux is always wrong
It removes the need for tests
It hides implementation details from reviewers

questions.explanation: Project-based learning values explaining tradeoffs, not just shipping code.

questions.prompt: A manual test script only checks the happy path. What should be added?

options.text: Edge cases such as empty input, API failure, invalid quantities, and reload behavior
Only screenshots of the home page

questions.explanation: Manual scripts should cover important edge cases from the project requirements.
